subject: Request: temporary SLA carve-out for filter/toolchain timeouts impacting structured output
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@finedge.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident impact + request for temporary SLA carve-out for filter/toolchain timeouts

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the quick ring last night. To recap: between 09:05–09:48 PT on 2028-09-20 you saw multiple failures where our content-filter step triggered a tool-call fallback, which in some paths caused structured-output validators to time out and the overall request to exceed your 250ms 95th-based latency SLO. You reported ~1.8% of generation requests for the FinEdge "policy-review" route returning an intermittent 502 or a truncated payload during peak load.

We ran an initial investigation and attached a filtered diagnostic log (diagnostic-log-20280920.txt) showing the filter timeouts and the downstream validator timeouts pinned to the same window. Root cause appears to be an overload of the filter tooling due to an atypical spike in payload size combined with a seldom-hit regex path. We have a fix to rate‑limit and stream longer prompts through a batched path, but that requires a config rollout and brief throttling of the affected filter nodes.

Because this is directly tied to the filter/toolchain and structured-output validation (not core model availability), and given the impact to your SLOs during the event window, we’d like to propose a temporary SLA carve-out for filter/tooling-induced latency/availability for the affected route while we roll out mitigations. The carve-out would: 
- be scoped to the FinEdge "policy-review" route only
- be valid for a five-day remediation window (2028-09-21 through 2028-09-25)
- include an operational mitigation plan (see attached PDF) and a scheduled patch rollout on 2028-09-22 02:00 PT with a fallback toggle if regressions are detected

If you accept, we’ll formalize the carve-out and provide a short credit calculation for the affected window; if you prefer not to accept a carve-out we’ll prioritize immediate throttling and a cold rollback plan (but that will likely cause brief elevated latency as we force all traffic through the slower safe-path).

I understand this hits the SLA calculus — wanted to get your view before escalating for formal leadership approval.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: diagnostic-log-20280920.txt (text/plain, filtered)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@finedge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: FinEdge Eng Ops <eng-ops@finedge.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 17:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident impact + request for temporary SLA carve-out for filter/toolchain timeouts

Alex —

Appreciate the quick summary. We saw the same window on our side and it caused two downstream automation jobs to fail validation; the engineering team had to run a manual retry. Impact was user-visible for ~30 minutes for a small subset of rules.

We need two things to sign off on a carve-out: 1) an explicit timeline and rollback criteria, and 2) assurance that credits will be offered if the issue repeats during remediation. Can you provide the credit math and the post-rollout monitoring playbook?

If you plan a hotfix on 09-22, please avoid changes during our trading hours (08:00–17:00 ET). Otherwise, the proposed scope and five-day window sounds reasonable.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations, FinEdge
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 08:33:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident impact + request for temporary SLA carve-out for filter/toolchain timeouts

Alex / Marcus —

Looping in Product/Infra perspective. Short answers:
1) Timeline & rollback: we can schedule the config rollout during the early maintenance window on 09-22 02:00 PT as proposed. Rollback can be executed quickly by toggling the new filter rate-limit to off; we estimate 8–12 minutes to revert traffic.
2) Monitoring & credits: we’ll provide a post-deploy playbook: p95/p99 latency dashboards, structured-output failure counter, and an automated alert that will trigger a rollback if failure rate > 0.8% for 10 consecutive minutes. If the failure contributes to a breach of your contractual 95th percentile SLO during the carve-out window we will offer a pro-rated credit equal to the impacted token charge for that window (standard credit methodology). I’ll attach a short draft credit calc to the carveout PDF.
3) Scope: we’ll limit the toggles to the "policy-review" route and ensure no changes to other FinEdge routes.

Marcus — please confirm the expected risk and the rollback timing here so Alex can present to FinEdge.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Sep 20, 2028 at 16:12, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the quick ring last night. To recap:...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@finedge.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident impact + request for temporary SLA carve-out for filter/toolchain timeouts

Grace / Alex / Samantha —

Short confirmation from Infra: risk is low for the limited rollout. Technical notes: the failure correlated to a rare regex path in the content filter that produces an O(n^2) cost for unusually long prompts. The planned mitigation will:
- introduce a pre-parse step that routes any prompt > 3.2k tokens to a streaming/batched filter path (reduces per-request amplification)
- add a per-node circuit-breaker to stop calling the validator after X consecutive tool timeouts and fallback immediately to the safe-path (some degradation in output fidelity possible)

Rollback will be a single toggle and we will warm the filter pool with staged traffic before hitting full production. If FinEdge approves, we’ll execute at 02:00 PT on 09-22 with a 60-minute verification window. If any regression is detected we’ll flip the toggle and notify immediately.

Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final: carve-out proposal and next steps (FinEdge policy-review route)

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per Grace and Marcus above, attached is the formal SLA carve-out proposal (sla-carveout-proposal.pdf) which includes: timeline, rollback criteria, monitoring thresholds, and the draft credit calculation. Key points:
- Scope: FinEdge "policy-review" route only
- Window: 2028-09-21T00:00:00Z — 2028-09-25T23:59:59Z (five-day remediation window)
- Rollout: 2028-09-22 02:00 PT with 60-minute verification; no changes during your trading hours
- Monitoring: automatic rollback if structured-output failure rate > 0.8% over 10 consecutive minutes
- Credits: pro-rated token-based credit if the breach is attributable to filter/tooling during the window (method in PDF)

Please reply with a one-line acceptance ("Approve carve-out") and we will: 1) formalize the carve-out amendment, 2) schedule the rollout with your ops calendar, and 3) share the live dashboard for the verification window.

If you prefer a stricter alternative, we can instead perform a forced throttling that eliminates the need for a carve-out but will increase median latency briefly as we route to the safe-path.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0123
